text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 8 in history.
1587 - After 19 years imprisonment, Mary Queen of Scots was beheaded for her part in a plot to overthrow Queen Elizabeth.
1725 - Peter the Great of Russia died, and was succeeded by Catherine I. His reign saw Russia drawn increasingly into the European sphere of influence.
1819 - John Ruskin, English writer and art critic, born. He championed the artist Turner and the pre-Raphaelites, before he turned his attention to politics and social injustice.
1820 - William Sherman, U.S. general during the Civil War and a major influence on modern warfare, born.
1828 - Jules Verne, French science fiction writer, born. His adventure novels like "Journey to the Centre of the Earth" and "Around the World in 80 Days", stressed the possibilities of science.
1861 - The southern states which had seceded from the Union agree to set up The Confederate States of America.
1894 - King Wallis Vidor, U.S. film director, born. His silent film, "The Crowd", is recognized as a masterpiece.
1920 - Lana Turner, U.S. actress, born as Julia Jean Mildred Francis Turner. Known as the "sweater girl", her most famous roles were in "The Postman Always Rings Twice" and "Peyton Place".
1921 - Peter Alekseivich Kropotkin, Russian revolutionary and geographer, died. In 1871 he gave up his scientific work and became a leader and theorist of anarchism.
1924 - The gas chamber was used for the first time as a form of execution. Gee Jon was put to death in Nevada for murder.
1925 - Jack Lemmon, U.S. film actor, born as John Uhler Lemmon III. Won two Oscars for his roles in "Mister Roberts" and "Save the Tiger".
1931 - James Dean, U.S. film actor and cult hero, born as James Byron. In "East of Eden" and "Rebel Without a Cause" he personified teenage rebellion.
1937 - In the Spanish Civil War, General Franco captured Malaga with the help of 15,000 Italians.
1942 - Dr Albert Speer succeeded Dr Fritz Todt as German minister for armaments and war production. Todt was killed in a plane crash.
1943 - Advancing Russian troops recaptured Kursk, which they had lost to the Germans in November 1941.
1949 - Cardinal Jozsef Mindszenty, Primate of Hungary, was sentenced to life imprisonment for anti-state activities.
1955 - Georgi Malenkov was forced to resign the Soviet premiership, replaced by Nikolai Bulganin.
1967 - Sir Victor Gollancz, publisher and writer, died. During the war he helped to get Jewish refugees out of Germany.
1974 - America's final Skylab mission, with Gerald Carr, Edward Gibson and William Pogue, returned to earth.
1983 - The Kahan Report on the Beirut Sabra and Shatila massacres in September 1982, condemned the Israeli government and Defence Minister Ariel Sharon.
1989 - A Boeing 707 crashed into a mountain on Santa Maria Island, The Azores.
1993 - The newly divided Czech and Slovak republics began using separate currencies for the first time.
